messages:
maya: Heads up — started seeing a persistent p99 jump on cluster-east-2 at ~08:12 UTC. Looks correlated with the microbatch/kernel rollout we pushed at 07:50. Dumping what I have so far.

maya: Quick profile snippet from a few traces (synth load + a hot prefix):
```
kernel_select: matmul_v2 -> matmul_scalar (fallback on certain seq-lens)
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.78 -> 0.42
concurrency: 520 -> 800 (clients autoscaled)
microbatch_size: 4 -> 8
p95: 40ms -> 85ms
p99: 120ms -> 420ms
observed_tail_events: eviction spikes + kernel fallback serialization
```

ops-bot: ALERT: anomaly-detect/latency p99 exceeded threshold on cluster-east-2 (08:13 UTC) :rotating_light:

zheng: Can you paste the exact rollout config we pushed? Also where did the kernel selector gate change live?

maya: Config blob we rolled: `{"microbatch":{"size":8,"batching_policy":"throughput"},"kernel_selector":{"enable_v2":true,"hysteresis_ms":10}}` — selector change was a small tweak to prefer matmul_v2 for batch sizes >=6.

sophia: If microbatch size increased occupancy of the shard-local KV, eviction pressure rises — that can cause frequent KV misses and rehydration which cascades into more work on the fallback kernel path. Combined with higher concurrency that smells like eviction storms.

jared: Agree. Two quick hypotheses: 1) hot-prefix churn — larger microbatches combine more prefixes so local hotset grows and crosses eviction threshold; 2) kernel fallback is slower and serializes GPU->CPU path, amplifying tail.

zheng: Any profiling of kv eviction events vs per-request latency? Even a histogram would help. Also share the eviction_policy and max_entries for the shard.

maya: Got a TL;DR from tracing: 70% of p99 events have an eviction within the last 30s on the same shard. Eviction policy is LRU, max_entries=65536.

sophia: Short-term mitigation options:
- roll back microbatch size to 4 (restore previous hotset footprint)
- increase max_entries to 98304 or bump HWM by 1.5x (risk memory pressure)
- enable kv_hysteresis: avoid evicting entries younger than 2s
- change kernel_selector to prefer v2 only for strict size match (avoid fallback path)

jared: Also try limiting client concurrency per-shard for a burst window (token bucket) while we triage. That prevents synchronized cache churn.

maya: I'll roll back microbatch to 4 for cluster-east-2 now and pin kernel_selector to the pre-rollout config. Rolling via admin API: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/rollout -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN}" -d '{"target":"cluster-east-2","changes":{"microbatch.size":4,"kernel_selector.hysteresis_ms":5}}'
```

deploy-bot: rollout/started cluster-east-2 by maya (rollout-id: r-2028a7)

maya: Rollback completed at 09:05 UTC. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: NOTE: p99 for the last 5m after rollback is trending down (p99 ~ 130ms), will keep 15m window open.

sophia: Great — after stabilization we should run a controlled A/B: vary microbatch sizes and measure (1) per-shard kv occupancy, (2) eviction rate, (3) kernel fallback rate, (4) end-to-end p95/p99. Prefer synthetic replay of production traces.

zheng: I'll schedule a perf sweep and add a small tracepoint to log `kv_eviction_reason` (hot_prefix|capacity|ttl) so we can break down why entries are leaving.

maya: Thanks team. Filing a short incident note and adding follow-up items to the postmortem board. :white_check_mark:
